name: Neuromyelitis Optica Spectrum Disorder without Anti-MOG and without Anti-AQP4 Antibodies

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: International Consensus Diagnostic Criteria for NMOSD (2015) - adapted for seronegative cases

criteria.description: At least one core clinical characteristic including optic neuritis, acute myelitis, area postrema syndrome, acute brainstem syndrome, symptomatic narcolepsy or diencephalic syndrome, or symptomatic cerebral syndrome with NMOSD-typical brain lesions
Negative testing for both anti-AQP4 and anti-MOG antibodies confirmed by validated assays
MRI findings consistent with NMOSD such as longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (LETM) or characteristic brain lesions
Exclusion of alternative diagnoses such as multiple sclerosis or other inflammatory disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of at least one core clinical characteristic, negative anti-AQP4 and anti-MOG antibodies, supportive MRI findings, and exclusion of alternative diagnoses
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is challenging due to seronegativity; clinical and radiological features are critical.

pathognomonic.notes: Spinal cord lesion extending over three or more vertebral segments
searchTerms: spinal cord swelling over multiple segments

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe optic neuritis with visual loss
pathognomonic.notes: Often bilateral and severe visual impairment
searchTerms: severe vision loss from optic nerve inflammation
optic nerve swelling with vision problems

common.symptomName: Area postrema syndrome with intractable hiccups or nausea
Acute brainstem syndrome with diplopia and dysphagia
common.notes: Brainstem involvement causing cranial nerve deficits
searchTerms: brainstem inflammation causing double vision and swallowing problems
acute brainstem symptoms with difficulty swallowing

common.notes: Often related to spinal cord lesions

searchTerms: problems with automatic body functions including low blood pressure when standing
autonomic nervous system dysfunction causing dizziness

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric symptoms such as depression or anxiety
rare.notes: Secondary to chronic illness or CNS involvement
searchTerms: psychiatric problems like sadness or worry

laboratory: CSF pleocytosis with mild lymphocytic predominance
Elevated CSF protein without oligoclonal bands typical of MS
imaging: MRI showing longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (≥3 vertebral segments)
MRI brain with lesions in area postrema, diencephalon, or brainstem
Absence of typical MS lesions on MRI
genetic: No known specific genetic mutations associated
other: Evoked potentials may show delayed conduction in optic nerves or spinal cord

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of oligoclonal bands in CSF
Typical periventricular brain lesions on MRI
Positive response to MS-specific disease-modifying therapies
More frequent cortical and subcortical lesions
Better prognosis and different treatment response
Often preceded by infection or vaccination

redFlags: Rapid onset of bilateral optic neuritis with severe visual loss
Longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis causing paralysis
Intractable nausea, vomiting, or hiccups indicating area postrema syndrome
references: Wingerchuk DM, Banwell B, Bennett JL, et al. International consensus diagnostic criteria for neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorders. Neurology. 2015 Jul 14;85(2):177-89.
Jarius S, Wildemann B. AQP4 antibodies in neuromyelitis optica: diagnostic and pathogenetic relevance. Nat Rev Neurol. 2010 Jul;6(7):383-92.
Flanagan EP, Weinshenker BG, Krecke KN, et al. Epidemiology and clinical features of neuromyelitis optica spectrum disorder without aquaporin-4 antibodies. JAMA Neurol. 2016 Sep 1;73(9):1110-1117.
